evidence.assessment: Live startup computes SHA256 directly from owner sources.enc bytes before read_planner. The before digest and ciphertext basis are written in an initial run record before case configuration or engine execution; after is null with pending status. No ciphertext or source credential is exported by the new fields.

Q06 selects the provider model-a identity independently of consumer selected peer identity. Every common provider_for lookup for that provider_selected re-reads the original owner path and rejects changed/unavailable bytes before installing inner transport. Mapping assertion and ModelDispatchAdapter type gate remain; only its inner transport is replaced. Both cohort branches use this installed gate.

Final after digest is independently calculated from current owner ciphertext bytes after llm_shutdown. Equality is evaluated against the startup digest. OSError records after=null, status=unknown, unchanged=false instead of reusing before or claiming equality.

Fixture mode leaves owner_path/hash unset, skips both owner reads, and records null before/after with not_applicable status and basis. unchanged=true is existing no-owner-applicable behavior, qualified by explicit not_applicable metadata.

Owner guard error strings remain limited to the two safe literal codes; arbitrary OSError messages/paths are not exported by these catches. Existing full record credential/reasoning export guard remains.

independent_validation.scope: Actual CLI orchestration with synthetic owner for normal/changed/deleted/unreadable final states and initialization record checks; fixture owner read forbidden; AST-extracted exact common gate with real outer ModelDispatchAdapter and offline counting inner; between-call drift; safe error-code export. No real model API.

limitations: Startup unreadability is fail-closed before an output directory/initial record exists; unknown/null recording applies to final re-read failure after a readable startup baseline. This patch does not add a startup-failure artifact collector.

The guard is a pre-dispatch byte observation, not a filesystem lock through the network request; equal endpoint hashes do not prove absence of transient ABA changes between observations. No such stronger claim is made.
The tests execute common gate and CLI orchestration without live engines; reference/Q06 live runs were not repeated.
Hashes are provenance of owner ciphertext bytes, not proof of decrypted semantic equality or provider identity by themselves. Production binding/permission/quota gates remain separate.
No production, test, or historical run/review was modified by this review; only this new review artifact was created. No held-out access.
